title: New Legal Thriller Movie Shows Pharma Dark Side
author: Martha Rosenberg
content:
![](https://www.counterpunch.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/etactics-
inc-5NlpmCvCjHk-unsplash-680x453.jpg)

Image by Etactics Inc.

What if you were an MD/researcher at a Top 10 medical school who came face-to-
face with a lethal side effect to a popular drug? But, when you tried to
reveal it, you were engulfed by a legal and professional character
assassination campaign that included threats against your academic position
and journal publishing history, physical surveillance by private investigators
and even a home break-in?

That is the basic plot of the newly released feature length movie thriller
“The Goose That Laid the Golden Egg,” adapted from a book by the same name by
Doug Bremner, MD. The book and movie are fictional accounts of blockaded
attempts to highlight depression and suicidal side effects of the popular acne
drug Accutane.

Would drugmakers spend millions to protect sales from the revelation of a
popular drug’s lethal side effect? Would they exploit NIH/FDA loopholes,
bastardize science and tolerate patient deaths to keep a drug selling? Would
they bribe doctors to prescribe a drug and hide its risk with vacations and
other “payola”?

Playing Dr. Jack Forteo, actor Andy Evans conveys his journey of vacillation
between medical certainty, doubt and human empathy expertly-as well as the
journey’s effect on Forteo’s family life and his own tortured memories of
childhood.

Playing Amanda Bellaconda, the mother who finds her school aged son dead from
a self-inflicted hanging from the mental effects of his acne drug and who
becomes a safety activist, Hannah Fierman is so engaging, you want to join her
mission.

(An especially dramatic moment comes when, after Forteo triumphs over his
Pharma censors, families in the courtroom hold up pictures of their deceased
loved ones.)

David de Vries as Red Leghorn, the irascible attorney on the trail of the
harms hidden by the drug’s manufacturer channels the memory of the larger-
than-life Lyndon Baines Johnson (”LBJ”) and other indomitable and unstoppable
figures still appearing in legal movies and dramas.

Prescription Drug Suicide Risks Continue to be Hidden

As Big Pharma and the “patient groups“ it funds and Big Insurance and Big Tech
capture news media, suicide is said to be down. It has actually never been
higher thanks to the dangerous “mental health” drugs industry now pushes for
conditions once considered minor or even nonexistent.

In the military world, a 2022 report from the Defense Suicide Prevention
Office revealed that there were more suicides in 2021 than any other year
since the September 11 attacks. According to Army Times, suicide deaths among
active-duty troops routinely given prescription drugs “climbed to its highest
level since the Great Depression — 36.18 per 100,000 soldiers.” Why are the
rising suicide rates virtually unreported? Ask Your Doctor ads fund the news.

The fictionalized death of Bellaconda’s son that begins “The Goose That Laid
the Golden Egg” brings to mind the death of another high schooler: Cody Miller
who took his own life in 2007 after being on the allergy drug Singulair for
just 17 days. Singulair ads declaring that “side effects are mild and vary by
age” were still running on TV after the tragedy.

The movie also brings to mind the suicide deaths of Doug Alsberge, MD and
Douglas Briggs, MD caused by taking the drug Neurontin (gabapentin) according
to their wives and told to this reporter.

“The Goose That Laid the Golden Egg,” is a much-needed dramatic depiction of
the way industry profits occlude patient safety and protection and the uphill
fight for drug accountability.
